verses.zh: 那时，以色列中没有王。但支派的人仍是寻地居住；因为到那日子，他们还没有在以色列支派中得地为业。
verses.en: In those days Israel had no king. And in those days the Danite tribe was looking for a place[NOTE:1] to settle because at that time they did not yet have a place to call their own among the tribes of Israel.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “an inheritance.”
Heb “because there had not fallen to them by that day in the midst of the tribes of Israel an inheritance.”

verses.zh: 但人从琐拉和以实陶打发本族中的五个勇士，去仔细窥探那地，吩咐他们说：「你们去窥探那地。」他们来到以法莲山地，进了米迦的住宅，就在那里住宿。
verses.en: The Danites sent out from their whole tribe five representatives,[NOTE:1] capable men[NOTE:2] from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and explore it. They said to them, “Go, explore the land.” They came to the Ephraimite hill country and spent the night at Micah’s house.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “The Danites sent from their tribe five men, from their borders.”
Heb “men, sons of strength.”
Heb “They came to the Ephraimite hill country, to Micah’s house, and spent the night there.”

verses.zh: 他们临近米迦的住宅，听出那少年利未人的口音来，就进去问他说：「谁领你到这里来？你在这里做甚么？你在这里得甚么？」
verses.en: As they approached[NOTE:1] Micah’s house, they recognized the accent[NOTE:2] of the young Levite. So they stopped[NOTE:3] there and said to him, “Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? What is your business here?”[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “When they were near.”
Heb “voice.” This probably means that “his speech was Judahite [i.e., southern] like their own, not Israelite [i.e., northern]” (R. G. Boling, Judges [AB], 263).
Heb “turned aside.”
Heb “What [is there] to you here?”

verses.zh: 他回答说：「米迦待我如此如此，请我作祭司。」
verses.en: He told them what Micah had done for him, saying,[NOTE:1] “He hired me, and I became his priest.”
notes: Heb “He said to them, ‘Such and such Micah has done for me.’” Though the statement is introduced and presented, at least in part, as a direct quotation (note especially “for me”), the phrase “such and such” appears to be the narrator’s condensed version of what the Levite really said.

verses.zh: 他们对他说：「请你求问　神，使我们知道所行的道路通达不通达。」
verses.en: They said to him, “Seek a divine oracle for us,[NOTE:1] so we can know if we will be successful on our mission.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Ask God.”
Heb “so we can know if our way on which we are going will be successful.”

verses.zh: 祭司对他们说：「你们可以平平安安地去，你们所行的道路是在耶和华面前的。」
verses.en: The priest said to them, “Go with confidence.[NOTE:1] The Lord will be with you on your mission.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in peace.”
Heb “In front of the Lord is your way in which you are going.”

verses.zh: 五人就走了，来到拉亿，见那里的民安居无虑，如同西顿人安居一样。在那地没有人掌权扰乱他们；他们离西顿人也远，与别人没有来往。
verses.en: So the five men journeyed on[NOTE:1] and arrived in Laish. They noticed that the people there[NOTE:2] were living securely, like the Sidonians do,[NOTE:3] undisturbed and unsuspecting. No conqueror was troubling them in any way.[NOTE:4] They lived far from the Sidonians and had no dealings with anyone.[NOTE:5]
notes: Or “went.”
Heb “who were in its midst.”
Heb “according to the custom of the Sidonians.”
Heb “and there was no one humiliating anything in the land, one taking possession [by] force.”

Heb “and a thing there was not to them with men.” Codex Alexandrinus (A) of the LXX and Symmachus read “Syria” here rather than the MT’s “men.” This reading presupposes a Hebrew Vorlage אֲרָם (ʾaram, “Aram,” i.e., Arameans) rather than the MT reading אָדָם (ʾadam). This reading is possibly to be preferred over the MT.

verses.zh: 五人回到琐拉和以实陶，见他们的弟兄；弟兄问他们说：「你们有甚么话？」
verses.en: When the Danites returned to their tribe[NOTE:1] in Zorah and Eshtaol, their kinsmen[NOTE:2] asked them, “How did it go?”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “They came to their brothers.”
Heb “brothers.”
Heb “What you?”

verses.zh: 他们回答说：「起来，我们上去攻击他们吧！我们已经窥探那地，见那地甚好。你们为何静坐不动呢？要急速前往得那地为业，不可迟延。
verses.en: They said, “Come on, let’s attack them,[NOTE:1] for[NOTE:2] we saw their land and it is very good. You seem lethargic,[NOTE:3] but don’t hesitate[NOTE:4] to invade and conquer[NOTE:5] the land.
notes: Heb “Arise, and let us go up against them.”
Codex Alexandrinus (A) of the LXX adds “we entered and walked around in the land as far as Laish and.”
Heb “But you are inactive.”
Or “be lazy.”
Heb “to go”; “to enter”; “to possess.”

verses.zh: 你们到了那里，必看见安居无虑的民，地也宽阔。　神已将那地交在你们手中；那地百物俱全，一无所缺。」
verses.en: When you invade,[NOTE:1] you will encounter[NOTE:2] unsuspecting people. The land is wide![NOTE:3] God is handing it over to you—a place that lacks nothing on earth!”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “When you enter.”
Heb “you will come to.”
Heb “broad of hands,” an idiom meaning “wide on both sides.”
Heb “a place where there is no lack of anything that is in the earth.”

verses.zh: 于是但族中的六百人，各带兵器，从琐拉和以实陶前往，
verses.en: So 600 Danites, fully armed, set out from Zorah and Eshtaol.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “They journeyed from there, from the tribe of the Danites, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, 600 men, equipped with weapons of war.”

verses.zh: 上到犹大的基列・耶琳，在基列・耶琳后边安营。因此那地方名叫玛哈尼・但，直到今日。
verses.en: They went up and camped in Kiriath Jearim in Judah. (To this day that place is called Camp of Dan.[NOTE:1] It is west[NOTE:2] of Kiriath Jearim.)
notes: Or “Mahaneh Dan”; the Hebrew term “Mahaneh” means “camp [of].” Many English versions retain the transliterated Hebrew expression, but cf. CEV “Dan’s Camp.”
Heb “behind.”

verses.zh: 他们从那里往以法莲山地去，来到米迦的住宅。
verses.en: From there they traveled through the Ephraimite hill country and arrived at Micah’s house.

verses.zh: 从前窥探拉亿地的五个人对他们的弟兄说：「这宅子里有以弗得和家中的神像，并雕刻的像与铸成的像，你们知道吗？现在你们要想一想当怎样行。」
verses.en: The five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish[NOTE:1] said to their kinsmen,[NOTE:2] “Do you realize that inside these houses are an ephod, some personal idols, a carved image, and a metal image? Decide now what you want to do.”
notes: Codex Alexandrinus (A) of the LXX lacks the phrase “of Laish.”
Heb “brothers.”

verses.zh: 五人就进入米迦的住宅，到了那少年利未人的房内问他好。
verses.en: They stopped[NOTE:1] there, went inside the young Levite’s house (which belonged to Micah),[NOTE:2] and asked him how he was doing.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “turned aside.”
Heb “Micah’s house.”
Heb “they asked him concerning peace.”

verses.zh: 那六百但人各带兵器，站在门口。
verses.en: Meanwhile the 600 Danites, fully armed, stood at the entrance to the gate.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “And the 600 men, equipped with the weapons of war…from the sons of Dan.”

verses.zh: 窥探地的五个人走进去，将雕刻的像、以弗得、家中的神像，并铸成的像，都拿了去。祭司和带兵器的六百人，一同站在门口。
verses.en: The five men who had gone to spy out the land broke in and stole[NOTE:1] the carved image, the ephod, the personal idols, and the metal image, while the priest was standing at the entrance to the gate with the 600 fully armed men.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “went up, went in there, took.”
Heb “600 men, equipped with the weapons of war.”

verses.zh: 那五个人进入米迦的住宅，拿出雕刻的像、以弗得、家中的神像，并铸成的像，祭司就问他们说：「你们做甚么呢？」
verses.en: When these men broke into Micah’s house and stole[NOTE:1] the carved image, the ephod, the personal idols, and the metal image, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?”
notes: Heb “These went into Micah’s house and took.”

verses.zh: 他们回答说：「不要作声，用手捂口，跟我们去吧！我们必以你为父、为祭司。你作一家的祭司好呢？还是作以色列一族一支派的祭司好呢？」
verses.en: They said to him, “Shut up! Put your hand over your mouth and come with us! You can be our adviser[NOTE:1] and priest. Wouldn’t it be better to be a priest for a whole Israelite tribe than for just one man’s family?”[NOTE:2]
notes: See the note on the word “adviser” in 17:10.
Heb “Is it better for you to be priest for the house of one man or for you to be priest for a tribe, for a clan in Israel?”

verses.zh: 祭司心里喜悦，便拿着以弗得和家中的神像，并雕刻的像，进入他们中间。
verses.en: The priest was happy. He took the ephod, the personal idols, and the carved image and joined the group.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and went into the midst of the people.”

verses.zh: 他们就转身离开那里，妻子、儿女、牲畜、财物都在前头。
verses.en: They turned and went on their way, but they walked behind the children, the cattle, and their possessions.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “They turned and went and put the children, the cattle, and the possessions in front of them.”

verses.zh: 离米迦的住宅已远，米迦的近邻都聚集来，追赶但人，
verses.en: After they had gone a good distance from Micah’s house, Micah’s neighbors[NOTE:1] gathered together and caught up with the Danites.
notes: Heb “the men who were in the houses near Micah’s house.”

verses.zh: 呼叫但人。但人回头问米迦说：「你聚集这许多人来做甚么呢？」
verses.en: When they called out to the Danites, the Danites[NOTE:1] turned around and said to Micah, “Why have you gathered together?”
notes: Heb “they”; the referent (the Danites) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 米迦说：「你们将我所做的神像和祭司都带了去，我还有所剩的吗？怎么还问我说『做甚么』呢？」
verses.en: He said, “You stole my gods that I made, as well as this priest, and then went away. What do I have left? How can you have the audacity to say to me, ‘What do you want?’”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “What is this you say to me, ‘What to you?’”

verses.zh: 但人对米迦说：「你不要使我们听见你的声音，恐怕有性暴的人攻击你，以致你和你的全家尽都丧命。」
verses.en: The Danites said to him, “Don’t say another word to us, or some very angry men[NOTE:1] will attack you, and you and your family will die.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “bitter in spirit.” This phrase is used in 2 Sam 17:8 of David and his warriors, who are compared to a bear robbed of her cubs.
Heb “and you will gather up your life and the life of your house.”

verses.zh: 但人还是走他们的路。米迦见他们的势力比自己强盛，就转身回家去了。
verses.en: The Danites went on their way; when Micah realized[NOTE:1] they were too strong to resist,[NOTE:2] he turned around and went home.
notes: Heb “saw.”
Heb “they were stronger than he.”

verses.zh: 但人将米迦所做的神像和他的祭司都带到拉亿，见安居无虑的民，就用刀杀了那民，又放火烧了那城，
verses.en: Now the Danites[NOTE:1] took what Micah had made, as well as his priest, and came to Laish, where the people were undisturbed and unsuspecting. They struck them down with the sword and burned the city.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “they”; the referent (the Danites) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The Hebrew adds “with fire.” This has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons because it is redundant in English.

verses.zh: 并无人搭救；因为离西顿远，他们又与别人没有来往。城在平原，那平原靠近伯・利合。但人又在那里修城居住，
verses.en: No one came to the rescue because the city[NOTE:1] was far from Sidon[NOTE:2] and they had no dealings with anyone.[NOTE:3] The city[NOTE:4] was in a valley near Beth Rehob. The Danites[NOTE:5] rebuilt the city and occupied it.
notes: Heb “it.” The Hebrew pronoun is feminine singular here, referring to the “city” (a grammatically feminine singular noun) mentioned in v. 27.
For location see Map1-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.
Heb “and a thing there was not to them with men.”
Heb “it.” The Hebrew pronoun is feminine singular here, referring to the “city” (a grammatically feminine singular noun) mentioned in v. 27.
Heb “They”; the referent (the Danites) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 照着他们始祖以色列之子但的名字，给那城起名叫但；原先那城名叫拉亿。
verses.en: They named it Dan after their ancestor, who was one of Israel’s sons.[NOTE:1] But the city’s name used to be Laish.
notes: Heb “They called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who had been born to Israel.”

verses.zh: 但人就为自己设立那雕刻的像。摩西的孙子、革舜的儿子约拿单，和他的子孙作但支派的祭司，直到那地遭掳掠的日子。
verses.en: The Danites worshiped[NOTE:1] the carved image. Jonathan, descendant[NOTE:2] of Gershom, son of Moses,[NOTE:3] and his descendants[NOTE:4] served as priests for the tribe of Dan until the time of the exile.
notes: Heb “erected for themselves.”
Heb “son.”

Several ancient textual witnesses, including some LXX mss and the Vulgate, support the reading “Moses” (מֹשֶׁה, mosheh) here. Many Hebrew mss have a nun (נ) suspended above the name between the first two letters (מנשׁה), suggesting the name Manasseh (מְנַשֶּׁה, menasheh). This is probably a scribal attempt to protect Moses’ reputation. For discussion, see G. F. Moore, Judges (ICC), 401-2.
Heb “sons.”

verses.zh: 神的殿在示罗多少日子，但人为自己设立米迦所雕刻的像也在但多少日子。
verses.en: They worshiped[NOTE:1] Micah’s carved image[NOTE:2] the whole time God’s authorized shrine[NOTE:3] was in Shiloh.
notes: Heb “they set up for themselves.”
Heb “the carved image that Micah had made.”
Heb “the house of God.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 18:1-6

1In those days there was no king of Israel; and in those days the tribe of the Danites was seeking an inheritance
for themselves to live in, for until that day an inheritance had not been allotted to them as a possession among the tribes of
Israel. 2So the sons of Dan sent from their family five men out of their whole number, valiant men from Zorah
and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and to search it; and they said to them, "Go, search the land." And they came to the hill country
of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and lodged there. 3When they were near the house of Micah, they recognized
the voice of the young man, the Levite; and they turned aside there and said to him, "Who brought you here? And what are you
doing in this place? And what do you have here?" 4He said to them, "Thus and so has Micah done to me,
and he has hired me and I have become his priest." 5They said to him, "Inquire of God, please, that we may know
whether our way on which we are going will be prosperous." 6The priest said to them, "Go in peace; your way in
which you are going has the Lord's approval."

18:1 "there was no king of Israel" This is the recurrent phrase of Judges 17-21.

▣ "in those days" This refers to the period before there was a king (i.e., Saul). Another historical marker
(Jdgs. 18:30) shows this was written or edited by later generations.

- period of monarchy

- period of Assyrian exile

▣ "the tribe of the Danites" Dan was allotted land in the south (cf. Jos. 19:41-46; Jdgs. 1:34-36), but
pressure from the Amorites and Philistines caused them to seek another inheritance (cf. Jos. 19:47). The unsettled
condition is reflected in the phrase "camp of Dan" (cf. Jdgs. 13:25; 18:12).

▣ "for until that day an inheritance had not been allotted to them as a possession among the tribes of Israel"
This is a strange statement in light of Jos. 19:40-46.

However, Jos. 19:47 mentions a city called "Leshem," which most scholars think is the "Laish" of
Jdgs. 18:7, 29. If this is so, then Joshua, in its final form, had to be written after the relocation of Dan to the north.

The other option is to translate this phrase as "the Danite tribe was looking for a place to settle because
at that time they did not yet have a place to call their own among the tribes of Israel" (NET Bible).

18:2 "valiant men" This could refer to

- nobility (i.e., social rank)

- military ability

- courage

See full note at Jdgs. 6:12.

18:3 "they recognized the voice" They recognized either his accent (Judah) or his specialized vocabulary
(i.e., Levite).

18:5-6 The five spies recognized this private shrine as a valid worship site of YHWH. They fully accepted
this Levite's ability to communicate with YHWH.

NASB
"Your way in which you are going has the Lord's approval"

NKJV
"May the presence of the Lord be with you on your way"

NRSV, MT
"The mission you are on is under the eye of the Lord"

NJB
"YHWH is watching over your journey"

JPSOA
"The Lord views with favor the mission you are going on"

LXX
"Your journey that on which you are going, is before the Lord"

Peshitta
"May the Lord prosper the errand on which you go"

18:6 Notice the liturgical use of YHWH. In Jdgs. 18:31 the shrine is called "the house of Elohim." This Levite
was asserting his credentials as a true priest of YHWH. He was a grandson of Moses.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 18:7-10

7Then the five men departed and came to Laish and saw the people who were in it living in security, after the
manner of the Sidonians, quiet and secure; for there was no ruler humiliating them for anything in the land, and they
were far from the Sidonians and had no dealings with anyone. 8When they came back to their brothers at
Zorah and Eshtaol, their brothers said to them, "What do you report?" 9They said, "Arise, and let us go
up against them; for we have seen the land, and behold, it is very good. And will you sit still? Do not delay to go, to enter, to
possess the land. 10When you enter, you will come to a secure people with a spacious land; for God has given
it into your hand, a place where there is no lack of anything that is on the earth."

18:7 "Laish" It (BDB 539 II) is also known as "Leshem" (BDB 546, cf. Jos. 18:47) and "Lus" in Egyptian texts. It is
north of Hazor and north of Kedesh on the eastern side of Jordan.

▣ "living in security" This means in an isolated spot. The closest national power was the Phoenicians (i.e.,
Sidonians).

The people are characterized as:

- quiet ‒ BDB 1052, KB 1641, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE; this root is used several times in Judges

- of the land ‒ Jdgs. 3:11, 30; 5:31; 8:28; 18:7, 27; Jos. 11:23; 14:15; 2 Chr. 14:1, 5, 6

- of a city ‒ 2 Kgs. 11:20; 2 Chr. 23:21

- secure ‒ BDB 105, KB 120, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

- the VERB can mean "trust," cf. Jdgs. 9:26

- the VERB can mean "rely," cf. 2 Kgs. 18:20, 21, 24

- the NOUN means "secure," cf. Jdgs. 8:11; 18:7; Deut. 12:10; 33:12, 28; 1 Sam. 12:11; 1 Kgs. 5:4;
Ps. 16:9 (sometimes translated in NASB as "unsuspecting")

▣

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA, Peshitta
"anyone"

NRSV
"Aram"

NJB, REB
"Aramaeans"

The MT has "adam" (BDB 9), which means "mankind" (i.e., NASB, "anyone"). There is often a
confusion between the "d" in Hebrew and the "r." The same textual question is in Jdgs. 18:28.

The UBS Text Project, p. 118, gives "anyone" a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

▣ The end of this verse is uncertain. It depends on how one translates "ruler" (UBS Text Project,
pp. 116-117, "power-holder").

18:8 "Zorah and Eshtaol" These are cities west of Jerusalem on the coastal plain in the original allocation
given to Dan.

18:9 This is similar to the report of the twelve spies in Numbers 13-14. Here, however, the tribe of Dan
responds with confidence that YHWH is with them (Jdgs. 18:6,10).

- arise ‒ BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal PARTICIPLE

- let us go up against them ‒ BDB 748, KB 828, Qal IMPERFECT used in a
COHORTATIVE sense

- do not delay ‒ BDB 782, KB 868, Niphal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- to go ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

- to enter ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

- to possess the land ‒ BDB 439, KB 441, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

18:10 "a spacious land" The ADJECTIVE (BDB 932) basically means "wide" or "broad." It is
not describing a large land but a land of freedom. In Hebrew thought that which is narrow or tight describes difficulties,
but that which is broad describes freedom, joy, lack of restraint.

▣ "for God has given it into your hand" This is the message of the five spies based on the Levite's words
in Jdgs. 18:6.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣ "a place where there is no lack of anything that is on the earth" This is theologically parallel to "it
certainly does flow with milk and honey," cf. Num. 13:27. It was an abundantly fertile place (possibly reflecting Deut. 8:9).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 18:11-13

11Then from the family of the Danites, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, six hundred men armed with weapons
of war set out. 12They went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. Therefore they called that place
Mahaneh-dan to this day; behold, it is west of Kiriath-jearim. 13They passed from there to the hill country of
Ephraim and came to the house of Micah.

18:11 "six hundred men" This number of military personnel shows that the entire tribe of Dan was on the
move north (cf. Jdgs. 18:21).

18:12 "Mahaneh-dan" This name (BDB 334) means "camp of Dan" and is used in Jdgs. 13:25 to show
that the tribe of Dan had not possessed its tribal allocation from Joshua.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 18:14-20

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 18:27-31

27Then they took what Micah had made and the priest who had belonged to him, and came to Laish, to a people
quiet and secure, and struck them with the edge of the sword; and they burned the city with fire. 28And there was
no one to deliver them, because it was far from Sidon and they had no dealings with anyone, and it was in the valley which is
near Beth-rehob. And they rebuilt the city and lived in it. 29They called the name of the city Dan, after the name of
Dan their father who was born in Israel; however, the name of the city formerly was Laish. 30The sons of Dan set
up for themselves the graven image; and Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to
the tribe of the Danites until the day of the captivity of the land. 31So they set up for themselves Micah's graven
image which he had made, all the time that the house of God was at Shiloh.

18:28 "Beth-rehob" It means "house of open space" (BDB 112, cf. Num. 13:21). This was the most
northern area seen by Moses' spies. Its location is unknown (cf. 2 Sam. 10:6).

18:29 The Canaanite city of Laish (or Leshem of Jos. 19:47) becomes the namesake of the tribe—"Dan"
(BDB 192; Dan means "judge").

18:30 "Gershom" Many scholars believe this name (BDB 177) was mentioned earlier in Jdgs. 17:7 (see
notes there). This list of ancestors was an attempt to justify or legitimize this northern shrine and its priest, as opposed
to sites in the south.

The name "Gershom" is first mentioned in Exod. 2:22.

▣ "Manasseh" The original text has "Moses" (UBS Text Project, p. 120, gives it an "A" rating, NRSV,
TEV, NJB, REB), but the rabbis inserted a "suspended nun" to show their horror at the Levite's actions.

The MT even inserted the vowels for Manasseh. The LXX has "Manasseh."

The Levite's name was "Jonathan" (BDB 220).

▣ "until the day of the captivity of the land" This is a reference to (1) exile by Tiglath-pileser II in 733 B.C.
(cf. 2 Kgs. 15:29) or (2) Sargon II's exile in 722 B.C. This shows that Judges was compiled by an editor, not one
eyewitness author.

▣ "the house of God at Shiloh" This dates the book's original production in the time of Samuel
(cf. 1 Samuel 1).

Shiloh (ABD, vol. 5, pp. 1213-1215) became a central worship site (cf. Jos. 19:51; Jdgs. 21:12-21;
1 Sam. 1:3). It was later abandoned (cf. Ps. 78:60; Jer. 7:12-15; 26:6-9). The priestly line of Eli will be rejected!

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why are chapters 17-21 included in Judges?

- How is this section supportive of a strong central government?

- Are all the characters of this account presented in a poor light? If so, why?
